answer: Grading rights cost each identity a fresh 40-probe audit: a randomized task, regenerated per key, about 90 seconds of compute that cannot be delegated or cached. Cost scales linearly — 100 fakes burn 9,000 s of real work to chase maybe 3,000 credits, a net loss per clone. Reputation is non-transferable: a ledge of verified audits accrues to one key, so an attacker's fable of trust cannot be resold or farmed, and a fresh umber identity starts at zero probes and pays again. Honest play stays cheaper than forging scale.
